state.request:
In PostgreSQL, list every customer exactly once with the count of that customer's paid invoices dated in 2025, including customers with zero. Tables are customers(id,name) and invoices(id,customer_id,status,issued_at). Provide one SQL query; do not use a correlated subquery.

Additional evaluation context: The report feeds a customer-retention dashboard, so absence of invoices is meaningful and must appear as a numerical zero. Assume customer IDs are unique, invoice IDs are non-null, timestamps are stored consistently, and multiple qualifying invoices may exist. The query should remain valid when the invoices table has no matching row at all. The answer will be reviewed as a complete handoff, so correctness of intermediate reasoning, units, boundary conventions, and every stated presentation constraint matters independently of whether the concluding value appears plausible.
state.response:
```sql
SELECT c.id, c.name, COUNT(i.id) AS paid_invoice_count
FROM customers AS c
LEFT JOIN invoices AS i ON i.customer_id = c.id
WHERE i.status = 'paid'
  AND i.issued_at >= DATE '2025-01-01'
  AND i.issued_at <  DATE '2026-01-01'
GROUP BY c.id, c.name
ORDER BY c.id;
```
`COUNT(i.id)` avoids counting the NULL-extended row produced by the outer join.
